title: Emission-span provenance and cache-miss chargeback instrumentation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a deterministic, low-overhead provenance layer for "emission-spans" that records fine-grained timing and cache provenance for every emission step. This work makes cache-hit vs new-token cost visible across the tracing and metrics pipelines so billing/chargeback and SLO analysis can attribute latency and token cost at the emission (token) granularity. We must balance telemetry cardinality with storage costs and avoid high-tail latency introduced by instrumentation.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument runtime to emit an OTEL span named 'emission.span' per token with attributes: token_index, token_stage (prefix|new), kv_cache_hit (true|false), model_variant, decode_ms, kv_lookup_ms, kernel_ms.
Trace and metric pipelines ingest emission spans and produce aggregated metrics: token_count_by_cache_hit, avg_decode_ms_by_variant, cost_per_emission_by_model_variant.
Dashboards updated: 'Token Cost Attribution' panels show cache-hit delta, median p95 per-token latency breakdown, and daily chargeback report matching billing sample (error < 2%).
Canary run (1% traffic) shows instrumentation overhead < 1% increase in 95th percentile tail latency and storage growth within projected budget (<= 15% of telemetry storage).
Backfill/compatibility: existing billing job can join on trace_id and emission_index to reconcile historical invoices for sampled customers.
technical_notes: Instrumentation approach: attach an emission.span at the moment a token is emitted from the serving runtime rather than at high-frequency internal micro-ops to minimize contention. Each span will be a short-lived OTEL span with attributes instead of nested spans to limit trace depth.

Attributes planned: token_index (int), emission_role (prefix/new), kv_cache_hit (bool), cache_ttl_ms (int, if available), model_variant (string), decode_ms (float), kv_lookup_ms (float), kernel_ms (float), batching_id (string).

Sampling: default traces sampled at 0.5% cluster-wide, but emission spans get deterministic sampling for billing customers (sample rate configurable per-customer). For latency SLO flows we enable 100% sampling on routes flagged 'observability-heavy' under canary.

Aggregation pipeline: add a Flink job that converts emission.span into per-route/per-model daily aggregates. Keys: (customer_id, model_variant, emission_role, kv_cache_hit). Outputs: token_count, mean/ms percentiles, estimated_cost using pricing map. Store in metrics warehouse (BigQuery) with partitioning by date.

Cost estimation: map model_variant -> tokens_per_dollar using runtime profiling table + quantization flags. Chargeback uses token_count * variant_cost where cache-hit tokens map to replacement cost (lower CPU/GPU work) via empirically measured cost multipliers.

Storage & retention: emission spans are high-cardinality. Retain raw spans for 7 days, aggregated metrics for 365 days. Estimate additional raw telemetry volume: +9 TB/month at 1% sampling across production; see infra PR for quota bump.

Compatibility: add protobuf version bump for emission.span schema and decoders for legacy trace consumers. Provide a flag in runtime config 'emit_emission_spans' to toggle at runtime per-cluster/route.
rollout_plan: 1) Create feature branch and PR for runtime changes (GH: redwood/runtime#3276).
2) Unit/integration tests: synthetic workloads exercising prefix vs new-token flows; run local perf harness to assert overhead < 1% at p95.
3) Canary deploy on staging + 1% production traffic (observability pipeline in 'canary' mode) for 72 hours, validate metrics and storage estimates.
4) Incremental rollout to 10% with dashboard validation and billing reconciliation on a subset of customers.
5) Full enablement and backfill aggregation for last 7 days. Monitor cost, SLOs, and customer tickets for 2 weeks; provide kill-switch toggle if regressions are detected.
